instruction.text: Select the brightest star to learn more about stars.

end.text: Stars are balls of gas that can be seen in the night sky.

instruction.text: Can you find the Sun? Select the Sun.

end.text: Fun fact: Sirius is the brightest star in our night sky and burns blue-white, which means it is much hotter than our Sun. It is also a lot bigger.

atoms.text: You may not know this, but our Sun is in fact a star. It is a yellow dwarf star and is 100 times larger than the Earth. This may seem enormous to us on Earth, but the Sun is actually only a medium-sized star. Betelguese, for instance, is a red supergiant star and is 700 times larger than our Sun.

This may seem enormous to us on earth, but the sun is actually only a medium-sized star. Bettle-jerz, for instance, is a red supergiant star, and is 700 times larger than our sun.

atoms.text: Our solar system is controlled by the gravity of the Sun. Its gravitational pull is what keeps the planets in our solar system in orbit. All planets in our solar system orbit around the Sun, meaning they slowly spin around the Sun in a circle. Earth orbits around the Sun, while the Moon orbits around the Earth. On Earth, one full orbit around the Sun equals one year.

text: Gravity is an invisible force that pulls things together. For example, in this picture you see an ice cream cone that has fallen on the ground. Gravity is what pulls the ice cream down to the ground.
hint.label: Gravity

atoms.text: The Sun is the nearest star to the Earth. Without the Sun, Earth would be very cold, and most life on Earth would not be able to exist. The Sun is extremely hot, about 5,500 degrees Celsius. However, not all parts of the Sun’s surface are the same temperature. If you look at the Sun’s surface, you can sometimes see darker spots. These are called sunspots. Sunspots are spots that are colder than the rest of the Sun’s surface.

instruction.text: True or false? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Sunspots are hotter than the rest of the Sun’s surface.
Sunspots are colder than the rest of the Sun’s surface.
The Sun is a yellow dwarf star.
